paper_verdict.estimator_family: Panel FE/RE/FGLS growth-accounting (Cobb-Douglas in growth rates) with IV-2SLS (lagged ICT) as robustness; headline is FE with robust Newey-West SEs
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Outcome is GDP growth (ΔlnY) and exposure is growth of ICT capital services, so coefficients are output elasticities in growth-rate form, not level elasticities or per-capita measures. Sub-period and full-sample/without-outlier estimates overlap the same data (not independent). Table 3 significance codes differ from Table 2. Text refers to IV results as 'Table 1' (typo). IV lags only mitigate simultaneity; authors conclude no indication of bias.

estimates.note: Table 2 col 1 (FE, without outliers). Unbalanced n = 27, N = 558. Outcome is GDP growth (ΔlnY); ICT = growth of ICT capital services.
Table 2 col 6 (FE, full sample): 0.116*** (0.02); N=567 matches note.
Table 2 col 4 (IV-2lags): 0.114*** (0.034); N=558 per Table 2 note. Text says first-stage F around 30.
Table 2 col 5 (IV-4lags): 0.095** (0.036); N=558 per Table 2 note (note applies to without-outliers sample).
Table 3 col 2005-2016 RE: 0.094* (0.029); N=320. Printed star level (*) is inconsistent with t about 3.2 under the table's own codes, but the coefficient and SE are as printed.

paper_verdict.estimator_family: Dynamic panel two-step system GMM (xtabond2, small) with ICT goods imports as external instrument
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Dynamic model with lagged dependent variable 0.9617, so coefficients are short-run effects with long-run multiplier about 26x; ICTMI is a composite index (fixed phone + 0.2 x mobile, broadband, fixed internet, users) in levels, not a log capital measure; ICTMI coefficient is conditional on an ICTMI x SERT interaction in the same model; outcome is log GDP per capita (labelled GNI in Table 4 header); 24 Asian countries of mixed income, only one specification reported. Text misreads coefficient magnitudes (e.g. 0.119% for 10% increase) and describes model with i=1..11. Instrument count 30 vs 24 countries exceeds the rule of thumb the authors cite.

estimates.note: Table 4 has separate Coefficients, Standard Errors, t-statistics, p-values columns; SE type correct. Obs. = 216, Countries = 24. Sample is Asian countries 2000-2010 (abstract says 2001-2010), mixed income (Japan, Korea, Israel with Bangladesh, Tajikistan, Yemen). Specification includes ICTMI x SERT interaction, so the ICTMI coefficient is the effect at zero tertiary enrolment, not an average effect; exposure is a level index (not log) and outcome is log GDP per capita in a dynamic model with lagged YPC coefficient 0.9617 (short-run effect). Table header calls the dependent variable Gross National Income, text defines YPC as log GDP per capita PPP.
Matches Table 4 row. This is the coefficient on the ICT x tertiary-enrolment interaction, not a main ICT effect; Obs. = 216, Countries = 24. Not poolable with main-effect elasticities.
